昂首闊步.d: Head raised and taking long steps: a proud, confident walk.
x: 冠軍昂首闊步走進球場。

s.d: Head up, chest out; about posture.
s.z: 上台時要抬頭挺胸，看著觀眾。
s.y: Stand tall and look the audience in the eye.

s.d: Swaggering with no regard for others; about attitude.
s.z: 他大搖大擺地走進會議室，彷彿這裡是他的地盤。
s.y: He swaggered into the meeting as if he owned the place.

a.z: 輸了比賽，大家垂頭喪氣地回家。
a.y: After losing the match, everyone went home dejected.

a.z: 老先生步履蹣跚地走著。
a.y: The old man walked unsteadily.

昂首闊步.u: Can describe an actual walk or confidently moving toward the future. Mostly positive, sometimes a bit proud.

把酒言歡.d: Raising a cup and chatting happily: friends enjoying drinks and good talk.
x: 老同學難得重聚，把酒言歡到深夜。

s.d: Toasts all round; about the scene at a banquet.
s.z: 席間觥籌交錯，氣氛熱烈。
s.y: Amid the clinking of glasses, the party grew livelier.

e: a good time was had by all
s.d: Hosts and guests alike enjoy themselves; about the result.
s.z: 晚宴在高潮中結束，賓主盡歡。
s.y: The dinner ended on a high note, and a good time was had by all.

a.z: 兩人為了錢爭吵，聚會不歡而散。
a.y: The two quarreled over money, and the gathering ended on a sour note.

a.d: Drinking to drown one's troubles; often alone or low.
a.z: 失戀之後，他天天借酒澆愁。
a.y: After the breakup, he drowned his sorrows in drink every night.

把酒言歡.u: For reunions of friends or old classmates, in a warm, relaxed mood. Leans toward heart-to-heart talk rather than the banquet scene.

杯盤狼藉.d: Cups and plates scattered about: a table in a mess after a banquet.
x: 宴會結束後，桌上杯盤狼藉。

s.d: A scene of utter mess; broader, for any place.
s.z: 颱風過後，街上一片狼藉。
s.y: After the typhoon, the street was a complete mess.

s.d: Full and content; about the diners, not the table.
s.z: 酒足飯飽之後，大家坐在院子裡聊天。
s.y: Once everyone was well fed, we sat in the yard and talked.

a.d: Bright windows and clean tables; spotless.
a.z: 房間窗明几淨，一塵不染。
a.y: The room was spotless, without a speck of dust.

杯盤狼藉.u: Describes the scene after a good meal. It can be teasing and is not always critical.

x: 四月時，花園一片奼紫嫣紅。

s.d: A riot of colors.
s.z: 春天讓山坡一片萬紫千紅。
s.y: Spring brought a riot of colors to the hillside.

s.d: Gorgeous and colorful.
s.z: 節慶服裝絢麗多姿。
s.y: The festival costumes were gorgeous and colorful.

奼紫嫣紅.u: Formal; for spring blossoms, found in Tang Xianzu's The Peony Pavilion.

沉魚落雁.d: Fish sink and geese fall at the sight: a woman of striking beauty.
x: 她美得沉魚落雁，走到哪裡都引人側目。

s.d: Beauty enough to topple a kingdom; more extreme.
s.z: 傳說中那位公主傾國傾城。
s.y: The princess was said to be a legendary beauty.

s.d: Born beautiful; about natural looks.
s.z: 她天生麗質，不太需要化妝。
s.y: She is a natural beauty and hardly needs makeup.

a.z: 他那副嘴臉實在面目可憎。
a.y: His sneering face was truly repulsive.

a.d: Plain-looking; a gentler way of putting it.
a.z: 他其貌不揚，卻有一身好本事。
a.y: He was plain-looking, but everyone admired his talent.

沉魚落雁.u: Often paired with a second idiom about the moon and flowers; together they sum up a beauty. An old exaggeration, now mostly literary or playful.

x: 這條鐵路穿越崇山峻嶺。

s.d: Range upon range of hills.
s.z: 山峰連綿，消失在霧中。
s.y: Range upon range of hills disappeared into the mist.

s.d: A long and tiring journey.
s.z: 他跋涉千山萬水，只為見她一面。
s.y: He made a long and tiring journey across mountains and rivers to see her.

崇山峻嶺.u: Formal; found in Wang Xizhi's Preface to the Orchid Pavilion Poems.

楚楚動人.d: Delicate, soft and appealing: someone who draws sympathy and affection.
x: 她身穿淡藍色洋裝，顯得楚楚動人。

s.d: Slender and poised; about stature.
s.z: 女兒長成了亭亭玉立的少女。
s.y: Her daughter has grown into a slender, poised young woman.

s.d: Born beautiful; about natural looks.

s.y: She is a natural beauty and hardly needs makeup.

a.z: 他那副嘴臉實在面目可憎。
a.y: His sneering face was truly repulsive.

a.d: Plain-looking; a gentler way of putting it.
a.z: 他其貌不揚，卻有一身好本事。
a.y: He was plain-looking, but everyone admired his talent.

楚楚動人.u: Mostly for a woman's tender grace and the wish to protect her. Rarely used of men.

垂涎欲滴.d: Saliva about to drip: food so tempting that one's mouth waters. It can also describe a strong craving for something.
x: 櫥窗裡的草莓蛋糕看起來垂涎欲滴。

s.d: Drooling over something, often greedily, with a hint of disapproval.
s.z: 孩子們對櫥窗裡的蛋糕垂涎三尺。
s.y: The kids were salivating at the cake in the window.

s.d: Appetite stirred; milder.
s.z: 夜市裡烤魷魚的香氣飄來，讓人食指大動。
s.y: The aroma of grilled squid at the night market was so appetizing that I joined the queue.

a.d: Bland and joyless, like chewing wax.
a.z: 沒加調味料，這碗湯喝起來味同嚼蠟。
a.y: Without any seasoning, the soup was bland and insipid.

a.z: 他最近食慾不振，什麼都吃不下。
a.y: He has been off his food lately and can hardly eat anything.

垂涎欲滴.u: Mostly for how food looks and smells. Used for gains or prizes, it can sound greedy.

炊煙裊裊.d: Smoke from cooking fires rising gently: a classic picture of home and village life at dusk.
x: 黃昏時分，村子裡炊煙裊裊。

s.d: Birdsong and the scent of flowers; about a spring landscape.
s.z: 春天一到，公園裡鳥語花香。
s.y: With spring here, the park was full of birdsong and blossoms.

e: beautiful scenery of lakes and mountains
s.d: Lakes and mountains set off each other; about natural scenery.
s.z: 這間飯店可以欣賞湖光山色。
s.y: The hotel offers beautiful scenery of lakes and mountains.

a.z: 這片沙漠荒無人煙。
a.y: The desert is desolate, without a soul in sight.

炊煙裊裊.u: A classic image of the countryside, with a warm, peaceful sense of everyday life.

大腹便便.d: A big, rounded belly: having put on weight, or heavily pregnant.
x: 一位大腹便便的中年男子坐在櫃檯前。

a.z: 大病一場之後，他變得骨瘦如柴。
a.y: After weeks of illness, he was skin and bones.

a.z: 她身材曼妙，穿什麼都好看。
a.y: She has a figure to die for; everything looks good on her.

大腹便便.u: Slightly teasing for a middle-aged man who has put on weight, neutral when describing a pregnant woman.

大快朵頤.d: Eating with great gusto, as if working one's cheeks with joy.
x: 爬完山，我們圍著一大鍋火鍋大快朵頤。

s.d: Eating fast and fiercely; about manners, not necessarily enjoyment.
s.z: 飢餓的孩子們狼吞虎嚥地吃完晚餐。
s.y: The hungry kids wolfed down their dinner.

s.d: Eating with obvious enjoyment; about the look of relish.
s.z: 學生們聽故事聽得津津有味。
s.y: The students listened to the story with great interest.

a.d: Unable to eat, usually because of mood or the food.
a.z: 聽到壞消息後，他食不下嚥。
a.y: After hearing the bad news, he could not eat a bite.

a.z: 他最近食慾不振，什麼都吃不下。
a.y: He has been off his food lately and can hardly eat anything.

大快朵頤.u: For the pleasure of a good meal. Light in tone and common in food reports.

大排長龍.d: People lined up like a long dragon: a very long queue.
x: 這家麵包店的鳳梨酥總是大排長龍。

s.d: Crowds like mountains and seas; about numbers, not necessarily a queue.
s.z: 廣場上人山人海，大家都來看煙火。
s.y: A vast crowd filled the square for the fireworks.

s.d: Every seat taken; about indoor places.
s.z: 今天早上座無虛席，真令人高興。
s.y: It is wonderful to see a packed house this morning.

a.z: 曾經擠滿人的購物中心，如今門可羅雀。
a.y: Once packed, the mall is now deserted.

大排長龍.u: For queues at famous shops, limited-edition goods and popular sights. The English idiom is line out the door.

大搖大擺.d: Swinging along carelessly, as though no one else is there.
x: 他大搖大擺地走進會議室，彷彿這裡是他的地盤。

s.d: Head high and striding; about confidence.
s.z: 冠軍昂首闊步走進球場。
s.y: The champion strode into the arena with his head held high.

s.d: Looking pleased with oneself; about mood.
s.z: 他得意洋洋地笑著，對勝利沾沾自喜。
s.y: He grinned, smug about winning.

a.z: 她躡手躡腳地走出房間，怕吵醒寶寶。
a.y: She tiptoed out so as not to wake the baby.

a.z: 她在走廊偷偷摸摸地打了一通電話。
a.y: She made a surreptitious call from the hallway.

大搖大擺.u: Often suggests not caring or ignoring others. Depending on context it can be critical, or simply describe an unconcealed attitude.

x: 這一區燈紅酒綠，盡是吃喝玩樂。

s.d: A life of decadence.
s.z: 這部電影描繪紙醉金迷的生活。
s.y: The film portrays a life of decadence.

s.d: Hustle and bustle.
s.z: 夜市裡熙來攘往，從不停歇。
s.y: The hustle and bustle of the night market never stops.

a.z: 曾經擠滿人的購物中心，如今門可羅雀。
a.y: Once packed, the mall is now deserted.

婀娜多姿.d: Soft, lovely bearing and light movements, as of a willow swaying: a graceful figure.
x: 舞者在舞台上婀娜多姿。

s.d: A lovely figure; about the shape, not the movement.
s.z: 她身材曼妙，穿什麼都好看。
s.y: She has a figure to die for; everything looks good on her.

s.d: Slender and poised; about how one stands.
s.z: 女兒長成了亭亭玉立的少女。
s.y: Her daughter has grown into a slender, poised young woman.

a.d: Burly and broad; the opposite of slender and soft.
a.z: 那位警衛虎背熊腰，看起來很有威嚴。
a.y: The bouncer was a burly man with broad shoulders.

婀娜多姿.u: Often for a woman's dancing and figure, and also for willow or flower branches swaying. Leans toward graceful movement.

肥而不膩.d: Fatty meat that still does not feel greasy: rich, fragrant and easy to finish.
x: 這道東坡肉肥而不膩，入口香濃。

s.d: Dissolves in the mouth; leans toward softness.
s.z: 這塊五花肉燉得入口即化。
s.y: The braised pork belly was melt-in-your-mouth tender.

s.d: Sweet without being cloying; about sweetness.
s.z: 這家的芋頭甜點甜而不膩，我一口氣吃了兩碗。
s.y: The taro dessert here is just sweet enough, never cloying, and I finished two bowls.

肥而不膩.u: For pork belly, goose and stews. Often paired with "sweet but not cloying" in food copy. Describing food, "unctuous" is a compliment.

風度翩翩.d: Graceful and elegant conduct, as if fluttering lightly: a man of outstanding poise.
x: 主人風度翩翩，讓每位賓客都如沐春風。

s.d: Carefree and debonair; leans toward temperament.
s.z: 王子風流倜儻。
s.y: The prince is dashing and debonair.

s.d: Handsome and upright; about appearance.
s.z: 他穿著合身的西裝，玉樹臨風。
s.y: He cut a dashing figure in his tailored suit.

a.z: 他不修邊幅、鬍子沒刮就來面試。
a.y: He turned up scruffy and unshaven for the interview.

風度翩翩.u: Mostly for a man's manner and speech. About poise rather than looks.

風捲殘雲.d: Like a gale sweeping away the last clouds: food cleared away fast and clean.
x: 一盤餃子端上桌，孩子們風捲殘雲，轉眼就吃光了。

s.d: Eating fast and fiercely; about manners.
s.z: 飢餓的孩子們狼吞虎嚥地吃完晚餐。
s.y: The hungry kids wolfed down their dinner.

s.d: Eating with gusto; about enjoyment, not necessarily speed.
s.z: 爬完山，我們圍著一大鍋火鍋大快朵頤。
s.y: After the hike, we feasted on a steaming hot pot.

a.z: 醫生建議用餐時要細嚼慢嚥。
a.y: The doctor advised chewing slowly and not rushing meals.

風捲殘雲.u: For eating something quickly until nothing is left. Often said as "like a gale sweeping the clouds".

x: 這座山谷草木蒼翠，富饒茂盛。

s.d: Exotic flowers and herbs.
s.z: 這座花園裡有許多奇花異草。
s.y: The garden is home to exotic flowers and herbs.

a.z: 戰後，大地滿目瘡痍。
a.y: After the war, the landscape was devastated and ravaged.

富饒茂盛.u: Formal; for land, plants and forests.

觥籌交錯.d: Wine cups and tally sticks crisscrossing: a lively banquet full of toasts.
x: 席間觥籌交錯，氣氛熱烈。

s.d: Chatting happily over drinks; about conversation, with a lighter mood.
s.z: 老同學難得重聚，把酒言歡到深夜。
s.y: Old classmates reunited and caught up over drinks until late.

e: a good time was had by all
s.d: Hosts and guests alike enjoy themselves; about the result.
s.z: 晚宴在高潮中結束，賓主盡歡。
s.y: The dinner ended on a high note, and a good time was had by all.

a.z: 兩人為了錢爭吵，聚會不歡而散。
a.y: The two quarreled over money, and the gathering ended on a sour note.

觥籌交錯.u: Formal, often used for banquets, year-end parties and weddings. The cups and tally sticks are old drinking-game gear.

鍋碗瓢盆.d: Pots, bowls, ladles and basins: the tools of a home kitchen.
x: 搬進新家前，她先買好了鍋碗瓢盆。

s.d: Daily necessities and chores; about household costs and housework.
s.z: 結婚後，他才懂得柴米油鹽的辛苦。

s.z: 在這裡停電是家常便飯。

鍋碗瓢盆.u: Also stands for the everyday work of running a household. It has a homey feel.

x: 這間茶館古色古香。

s.d: Picturesque.
s.z: 這個村莊如詩如畫。
s.y: The village is picturesque.

a.z: 這套軟體已陳舊過時。
a.y: The software suffers from obsolescence.

骨瘦如柴.d: Thin as firewood, nothing but bones: extremely emaciated.
x: 大病一場之後，他變得骨瘦如柴。

s.y: Chronic malnutrition left the children gaunt and pale.

s.d: Frail; about weakness.

s.y: She looked frail in the cold.

a.y: The bouncer was a burly man with broad shoulders.

a.z: 一位大腹便便的中年男子坐在櫃檯前。
a.y: A paunchy middle-aged man sat at the counter.

骨瘦如柴.u: For extreme thinness from illness or hunger. Take care when describing someone's body, as it can offend.

鶴立雞群.d: A crane standing among chickens: someone who clearly stands out in looks or talent.
x: 她身材高挑，氣質出眾，在人群中鶴立雞群。

s.d: Surpassing others in talent or character; about ability.
s.z: 即使在資優班裡，她的成績也出類拔萃。
s.y: Her grades are outstanding, even in a class of top students.

s.d: Having a style of one's own; about distinctiveness.
s.z: 這家餐廳融合台菜與法菜，獨樹一幟。
s.y: The restaurant is unique in its blend of Taiwanese and French cooking.

a.d: Ordinary, with nothing special about it.
a.z: 那只是辦公室裡平淡無奇的一天。
a.y: It was just a run-of-the-mill day at the office.

虎背熊腰.d: A back like a tiger and a waist like a bear: a big, sturdy build.

盡收眼底.u: For looking out from a height.
